cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# stockroom

A small tool for a shop run from plain-text files. It reads three files and answers three
questions: what is on the shelves and what needs buying, what an order costs, and what can be
shipped today.

It is a Python library (`import stockroom`) and a `stockroom` command. It needs Python 3.9 or
newer and uses only the standard library.

## Install

```
pip install .
```

This installs the importable `stockroom` package and the `stockroom` command. You can also run
`python -m stockroom` from a source checkout with `PYTHONPATH=src`.

## The three files

All three live in one folder: the current folder, or the one given with `--dir`. They are UTF-8;
a leading byte order mark is ignored; a line ends at LF or CRLF and nowhere else. Blank lines and
lines starting with `#` (after any spaces or tabs) are ignored. Anything else that breaks the
rules is a mistake, reported with the file name and the line number (counting from 1, blank and
comment lines included).

**`catalog.txt`** — one product per line, fields separated by `|`:

```
# SKU   | name            | price | reorder | tax
AB-100 | Garden gnome     | 12.50 | 5       | standard
cd-205 | Seed packet, mix | 1.99  | 40      | reduced
EF-310 | Gift voucher     | 25.00 | 0
```

SKU is two to four letters, a dash and three digits (shown in upper case, unique in any case).
The name is not empty and has no `|`. The price is at least `0.01` with at most two decimals.
Reorder is a whole number, zero or more. Tax is optional: `standard` (20 %, the default),
`reduced` (5 %) or `zero`, in any case.

**`movements.txt`** — stock in and out, one per line: `DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]`.

```
2024-03-01 AB-100 +20 first delivery
2024-03-04 ab-100 -3 order SO-1001
2024-03-05 CD-205 40
```

The date must exist, the SKU must be in the catalogue, the quantity is a non-zero whole number
(positive is stock in, negative is stock out). The note is the rest of the line, trimmed.
Movements count in date order (same-day movements keep file order); stock may never go below
zero at any point, and the line that takes it below zero is the mistake.

**`orders.txt`** — one order per line: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER LINES`.

```
SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme AB-100*12,CD-205*3
SO-1002 2024-03-09 Bea ab-100*2
```

The order number is `SO-` and digits, unique (`SO-7` and `SO-007` are different orders). The
customer is one word. Lines are `SKU*QUANTITY` separated by commas; each SKU is in the catalogue
and appears once, and the quantity is 1 or more.

A missing `catalog.txt` is an error for every command; a missing `movements.txt` or `orders.txt`
counts as empty. Each command reads only the files it needs: `stock`, `low`, `history`,
`receive` and `ship` read the catalogue and movements; `quote` reads the catalogue and orders;
`fulfil`, `invoice` and `report` read all three.

## Commands

Every command accepts `--dir DIR` (or `--dir=DIR`) anywhere on the line. Options are spelled in
full; abbreviations are not accepted.

```
$ stockroom stock
AB-100 17 ok Garden gnome
CD-205 40 low Seed packet, mix
EF-310 0 out Gift voucher

$ stockroom quote SO-1001
SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme
AB-100 12 12.50 150.00 -7.50 142.50
CD-205 3 1.99 5.97 0.00 5.97
subtotal 148.47
order discount 0.00
tax 28.80
total 177.27
```

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `stockroom stock [--json]` | `SKU ONHAND STATUS NAME` per product, by SKU. Status is `out` at zero, `low` when at or under the reorder level, else `ok`. |
| `stockroom low [--json]` | `SKU ONHAND REORDER BUY` for each `low` or `out` product; BUY is `max(1, 2 × reorder − onhand)`. |
| `stockroom history SKU [--json]` | `DATE DELTA BALANCE NOTE` for each movement of the product, in counting order. Unknown SKU is refused. |
| `stockroom receive DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` | Appends a stock-in movement to `movements.txt` and prints the line added. |
| `stockroom ship DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` | The same for stock out. |
| `stockroom quote ORDER [--json]` | Prices an order (see below). |
| `stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE` | Ships what the shelves can cover on DATE and records it. |
| `stockroom invoice ORDER [--json]` | Like `quote` but for the quantities shipped so far. |
| `stockroom report [--format text\|csv\|json]` | One row per order. |

`receive` and `ship` take the quantity as a whole number of one or more with no sign, and one
optional note (pass it as a single quoted argument; it may not contain a line break). A movement
that would break a rule (unknown SKU, bad quantity, stock below zero at any point in date order)
is refused and `movements.txt` is left byte-for-byte unchanged. If the file does not end in a
newline, one is added first. `receive`, `ship` and `fulfil` take no options except `--dir`: every
other argument is taken as typed, so `-3` is a bad quantity and `-5 oops` is a fine note.

`fulfil ORDER DATE` works out, per order line, what is still owed (quantity ordered less what
earlier shipments sent: negative movements for that SKU whose note is exactly `order SO-1001`).
It ships as many as the stock allows on DATE: no more than the stock after all movements dated on
or before DATE, and no more than the lowest stock at any later point. It appends one movement
`DATE SKU -N order SO-1001` per line shipped, prints `SKU shipped N backordered M` per line and
then `status open`, `status partial` or `status complete`. DATE before the order date is refused.

`invoice` prints `invoice ` before the header line and leaves out lines with nothing shipped; an
order with nothing shipped is refused. `report` text rows are
`ORDER DATE CUSTOMER STATUS SHIPPED/ORDERED QUOTED INVOICED`, sorted by date then order number;
`csv` has the header `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`; `json` is an
array of objects with the same keys (units as numbers, amounts as two-decimal strings).

### JSON

`stock` gives `{"sku", "name", "onhand", "status"}` objects, `low` gives
`{"sku", "onhand", "reorder", "buy"}`, `history` gives `{"date", "delta", "balance", "note"}`
(`delta` is a signed string such as `"+20"`), and `quote` / `invoice` give an object with `order`,
`date`, `customer`, `lines` (`sku`, `quantity`, `unit`, `gross`, `discount`, `net`), `subtotal`,
`order_discount`, `tax` and `total`. Amounts are strings with two decimals.

### Exit status

* `0` — it worked.
* `1` — a data file has a mistake, or the request is refused (unknown SKU or order, a movement
  that would break a rule, nothing shipped). The message on standard error names the file and
  line where there is one; nothing is written to standard output.
* `2` — a file cannot be read (missing `catalog.txt`, a folder that does not exist, bytes that
  are not UTF-8) or the command line is wrong (no or unknown command, wrong number of arguments,
  unknown option, bad option value, a mistyped date). The command line is checked before any file
  is read.

If the reader of the output goes away (`stockroom stock | head -1`) the command stops quietly with
status `0`.

## Prices

All amounts are exact to the penny and every rounding step rounds halves up.

1. A line's gross is quantity × unit price.
2. A line gets a volume discount of 5 % of its gross at quantity 10 or more, 10 % at 50 or more
   (not both), rounded to the penny. Net is gross less the discount.
3. The subtotal is the sum of nets. At £500.00 or more the order gets a 3 % order discount of the
   subtotal, rounded to the penny.
4. The order discount is shared over the lines in proportion to their nets: each share is rounded
   down and the leftover pennies go one each to the lines that lost the biggest fraction of a
   penny (the earlier line on a tie). A line's taxable amount is its net less its share.
5. Tax is worked out per line on its taxable amount at its product's rate, rounded to the penny,
   and added up. Prices do not include tax.
6. Total = subtotal + order discount (negative) + tax.

## Library

```python
import stockroom

catalog = stockroom.parse_catalog(open("catalog.txt", encoding="utf-8").read())
moves = stockroom.parse_movements(open("movements.txt", encoding="utf-8").read(), catalog)
orders = stockroom.parse_orders(open("orders.txt", encoding="utf-8").read(), catalog)
print(stockroom.stock_levels(catalog, moves))
quote = stockroom.price_order(orders[0], catalog)
print(quote.total)
```

* `parse_catalog(text)` returns a dict of upper-case SKU to a product with `.sku`, `.name`,
  `.price` (`Decimal`), `.reorder` (`int`) and `.tax`.
* `parse_movements(text, catalog)` returns movements in file order with `.date`
  (`datetime.date`), `.sku`, `.quantity` (`int`) and `.note` (`""` when there is none).
* `parse_orders(text, catalog)` returns orders in file order with `.id`, `.date`, `.customer`
  and `.lines`, a list of `(sku, quantity)` pairs.
* `stock_levels(catalog, movements)` is a dict of SKU to quantity on the shelf for every product.
* `price_order(order, catalog)` returns a quote with `.lines` (each with `.sku`, `.quantity`,
  `.unit`, `.gross`, `.discount`, `.net`), `.subtotal`, `.order_discount`, `.tax` and `.total`,
  all two-decimal `Decimal`s. Any object with `.lines` of `(sku, quantity)` pairs can be priced.
* A mistake in any text raises `stockroom.ParseError`, a `ValueError` with a `.line` attribute;
  its message contains `line N`. The library raises without a file name (`.filename` is `None`).

## Tests

```
python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

The suite uses only the standard library. It includes end-to-end tests that run
`python -m stockroom` against temporary folders, and one that runs `pip install .` into a fresh
virtual environment (this needs network access for the build backend).

import datetime
import unittest

import helpers  # noqa: F401  (puts src/ on sys.path)
from stockroom import parse_catalog, parse_movements, stock_levels
from stockroom.shelves import buy_quantity, format_delta, history, status
from stockroom.textio import ParseError, logical_lines

CAT = parse_catalog("AB-100|a|1|5\nCD-205|b|1|0")


class StatusTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_status(self):
        self.assertEqual(status(0, 5), "out")
        self.assertEqual(status(0, 0), "out")
        self.assertEqual(status(1, 5), "low")
        self.assertEqual(status(5, 5), "low")
        self.assertEqual(status(6, 5), "ok")
        self.assertEqual(status(1, 0), "ok")

    def test_buy_quantity(self):
        self.assertEqual(buy_quantity(0, 5), 10)
        self.assertEqual(buy_quantity(3, 5), 7)
        self.assertEqual(buy_quantity(5, 5), 5)
        self.assertEqual(buy_quantity(0, 0), 1)
        self.assertEqual(buy_quantity(9, 5), 1)

    def test_format_delta(self):
        self.assertEqual(format_delta(20), "+20")
        self.assertEqual(format_delta(-3), "-3")


class HistoryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_running_balance_in_count_order(self):
        moves = parse_movements(
            "2024-01-02 AB-100 -2 b\n2024-01-01 AB-100 +5\n2024-01-01 CD-205 +9\n2024-01-02 AB-100 +1 c\n", CAT)
        entries = history("AB-100", moves)
        self.assertEqual([(e.date, e.delta, e.balance, e.note) for e in entries], [
            (datetime.date(2024, 1, 1), 5, 5, ""),
            (datetime.date(2024, 1, 2), -2, 3, "b"),
            (datetime.date(2024, 1, 2), 1, 4, "c"),
        ])
        self.assertEqual(history("CD-205", moves)[0].balance, 9)

    def test_levels_follow_catalog_sorted(self):
        cat = parse_catalog("zz-900|z|1|0\nab-100|a|1|0")
        self.assertEqual(list(stock_levels(cat, [])), ["AB-100", "ZZ-900"])


class TextioTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_logical_lines_numbering_and_trim(self):
        text = "﻿# c\r\n\r\n  \t\r\n  a b \t\r\n#x\nlast"
        self.assertEqual(logical_lines(text), [(4, "a b"), (6, "last")])

    def test_only_lf_splits(self):
        self.assertEqual(logical_lines("a\rb\x0bc\x1cd e\x85f"), [(1, "a\rb\x0bc\x1cd e\x85f")])

    def test_single_bom_and_single_cr_dropped(self):
        self.assertEqual(logical_lines("﻿﻿a\r\r\n"), [(1, "﻿a\r")])

    def test_parse_error_filename_text(self):
        error = ParseError(7, "bad", "movements.txt")
        self.assertEqual(str(error), "movements.txt: line 7: bad")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""The same command line behaviour, driven in-process through stockroom.cli.main."""
import contextlib
import io
import json
import os
import tempfile
import unittest

import helpers  # noqa: F401  (puts src/ on sys.path)
from helpers import CATALOG, MOVEMENTS, ORDERS
from stockroom import cli
from stockroom.cli import UsageError, main, parse_args


class Capture:
    def __init__(self):
        self.out = io.TextIOWrapper(io.BytesIO(), encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        self.err = io.StringIO()

    def stdout(self):
        self.out.flush()
        return self.out.buffer.getvalue().decode("utf-8")


class InProcess(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        self.dir = self._tmp.name
        for name, text in (("catalog.txt", CATALOG), ("movements.txt", MOVEMENTS), ("orders.txt", ORDERS)):
            self.write(name, text)

    def write(self, name, text):
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, name), "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(text.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(text, str) else text)

    def read(self, name):
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, name), "rb") as handle:
            return handle.read()

    def run_main(self, *args):
        cap = Capture()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(cap.out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(cap.err):
            code = main(list(args) + ["--dir", self.dir])
        return code, cap.stdout(), cap.err.getvalue()

    def test_history(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main("history", "ab-100")
        self.assertEqual((code, err), (0, ""))
        self.assertEqual(out, "2024-03-01 +20 20 first delivery\n2024-03-04 -3 17 order SO-1001\n")
        code, out, err = self.run_main("history", "CD-205", "--json")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(out), [{"date": "2024-03-05", "delta": "+40", "balance": 40, "note": ""}])

    def test_history_unknown_sku(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main("history", "ZZ-999")
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (1, ""))
        self.assertIn("ZZ-999", err)

    def test_stock_and_low(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main("stock")
        self.assertEqual(out.splitlines()[0], "AB-100 17 ok Garden gnome")
        code, out, err = self.run_main("low", "--json")
        self.assertEqual([r["sku"] for r in json.loads(out)], ["CD-205", "EF-310"])

    def test_receive_and_ship(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main("receive", "2024-03-06", "ef-310", "4", " restock ")
        self.assertEqual((code, out, err), (0, "2024-03-06 EF-310 +4 restock\n", ""))
        code, out, err = self.run_main("ship", "2024-03-07", "EF-310", "4", "-1 dash note")
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (0, "2024-03-07 EF-310 -4 -1 dash note\n"))
        self.assertTrue(self.read("movements.txt").endswith(
            b"2024-03-06 EF-310 +4 restock\n2024-03-07 EF-310 -4 -1 dash note\n"))

    def test_refusal_leaves_file(self):
        before = self.read("movements.txt")
        for args in (("ship", "2024-03-06", "EF-310", "1"), ("ship", "2024-03-06", "AB-100", "-1"),
                     ("receive", "2024-03-06", "XX-000", "1"), ("receive", "2024-03-06", "AB-100", "1", "a\nb")):
            code, out, err = self.run_main(*args)
            self.assertEqual((code, out), (1, ""), args)
            self.assertTrue(err.startswith("stockroom: "), args)
        self.assertEqual(self.read("movements.txt"), before)

    def test_unencodable_note_refused(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main("receive", "2024-03-06", "AB-100", "1", "bad\udcff")
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (1, ""))

    def test_parse_error_names_file_and_line(self):
        self.write("movements.txt", "\n2024-03-01 AB-100 0\n")
        code, out, err = self.run_main("stock")
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (1, ""))
        self.assertIn("movements.txt: line 2", err)

    def test_file_problems_exit_2(self):
        os.remove(os.path.join(self.dir, "catalog.txt"))
        code, out, err = self.run_main("stock")
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (2, ""))
        self.assertIn("catalog.txt", err)

    def test_quote_fulfil_invoice_report(self):
        code, out, _ = self.run_main("quote", "SO-1001")
        self.assertTrue(out.endswith("total 177.27\n"))
        code, out, _ = self.run_main("fulfil", "SO-1001", "2024-03-03")
        self.assertEqual(out.splitlines()[-1], "status partial")
        code, out, _ = self.run_main("invoice", "SO-1001")
        self.assertTrue(out.startswith("invoice SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme\n"))
        code, out, _ = self.run_main("report", "--format", "csv")
        self.assertEqual(out.splitlines()[1], "SO-1001,2024-03-03,acme,partial,15,12,177.27,171.00")

    def test_broken_pipe_is_quiet(self):
        real_devnull = os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY)
        self.addCleanup(os.close, real_devnull)

        class Gone(io.RawIOBase):
            def writable(self):
                return True

            def write(self, data):
                raise BrokenPipeError()

            def fileno(self):
                return real_devnull

        stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(io.BufferedWriter(Gone()), encoding="utf-8")
        saved = os.dup2
        calls = []
        cli.os.dup2 = lambda src, dst: calls.append((src, dst))
        try:
            with contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout), contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()) as err:
                code = main(["stock", "--dir", self.dir])
        finally:
            cli.os.dup2 = saved
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertEqual(err.getvalue(), "")
        self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1)


class ParseArgsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def bad(self, *argv):
        with self.assertRaises(UsageError, msg=argv):
            parse_args(list(argv))

    def test_good(self):
        args = parse_args(["--dir=x", "stock", "--json"])
        self.assertEqual((args.command, args.directory, args.json, args.positionals), ("stock", "x", True, []))
        args = parse_args(["report", "--format=csv", "--dir", "y"])
        self.assertEqual((args.format, args.directory), ("csv", "y"))
        args = parse_args(["history", "-", "--json"])
        self.assertEqual(args.positionals, ["-"])

    def test_literal_commands(self):
        args = parse_args(["ship", "2024-01-01", "AB-100", "3", "--json", "--dir", "d", "-x"])
        self.assertEqual(args.positionals, ["2024-01-01", "AB-100", "3", "--json", "-x"])
        self.assertEqual(args.directory, "d")
        args = parse_args(["fulfil", "SO-1", "2024-01-01"])
        self.assertEqual(args.positionals, ["SO-1", "2024-01-01"])

    def test_bad(self):
        self.bad()
        self.bad("nope")
        self.bad("--json")
        self.bad("stock", "-x")
        self.bad("stock", "--json", "extra")
        self.bad("--dir")
        self.bad("report", "--format", "yaml")
        self.bad("report", "--format")
        self.bad("history")
        self.bad("fulfil", "SO-1", "2024-02-30")
        self.bad("receive", "2024-02-30", "AB-100", "1")
        self.bad("ship", "--json", "2024-01-01", "AB-100", "1")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

class InternalsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Direct calls into the helpers behind main()."""

    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        self.dir = self._tmp.name
        for name, text in (("catalog.txt", CATALOG), ("movements.txt", MOVEMENTS), ("orders.txt", ORDERS)):
            with open(os.path.join(self.dir, name), "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(text)

    def test_read_file(self):
        self.assertEqual(cli.read_file(self.dir, "catalog.txt", True), CATALOG)
        self.assertIsNone(cli.read_file(self.dir, "absent.txt", False))
        with self.assertRaises(cli.FileProblem):
            cli.read_file(self.dir, "absent.txt", True)
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "bin.txt"), "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(b"\xff")
        with self.assertRaises(cli.FileProblem):
            cli.read_file(self.dir, "bin.txt", False)

    def test_parse_file_names_the_file(self):
        with self.assertRaises(cli.Refusal) as caught:
            cli.parse_file("catalog.txt", cli.parse_catalog, "\nbad")
        self.assertEqual(str(caught.exception), "catalog.txt: line 2: expected 4 or 5 fields separated by '|'")

    def test_world_reads_what_the_command_needs(self):
        args = cli.Args("quote", ["SO-1001"], self.dir, False, "text")
        world = cli.World(args)
        self.assertEqual(world.movements, [])
        self.assertEqual(world.find_order("so-1002").customer, "Bea")
        with self.assertRaises(cli.Refusal):
            world.find_order("SO-3")
        args = cli.Args("stock", [], self.dir, False, "text")
        world = cli.World(args)
        self.assertEqual(world.orders, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(world.movements), 3)
        with self.assertRaises(cli.FileProblem):
            cli.World(cli.Args("stock", [], os.path.join(self.dir, "nope"), False, "text"))

    def test_append_movements_validates_whole_file(self):
        world = cli.World(cli.Args("stock", [], self.dir, False, "text"))
        with self.assertRaises(cli.Refusal):
            world.append_movements(["2024-03-06 EF-310 -1"])
        world.append_movements(["2024-03-06 EF-310 +1", "2024-03-06 EF-310 -1"])
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "movements.txt"), encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            self.assertEqual(handle.read(), MOVEMENTS + "2024-03-06 EF-310 +1\n2024-03-06 EF-310 -1\n")

    def test_output_helpers(self):
        self.assertEqual(cli.lines_out(["a", "b"]), "a\nb\n")
        self.assertEqual(cli.lines_out([]), "")
        self.assertEqual(cli.dump_json({"a": "é"}), '{\n  "a": "é"\n}\n')
        self.assertEqual(cli.dump_json([]), "[]\n")
EOF

cat > /tmp/prbody.md <<'EOF'
## Summary

Builds the whole `stockroom` tool from PRD #1: a Python 3.9+ standard-library package that is both an importable library and a `stockroom` console command (`pip install .`).
